_comment: Example for `agent-network-mcp ui --runners runners.json`: three Claude Code agents on a project in git, one worktree each.
Copy it (e.g. to agent-network-mcp/runners.json, which is gitignored) and replace every /abs/path with your paths.
Worktrees: cd /abs/path/project && git worktree add ../project-backend -b swarm-backend && git worktree add ../project-reviewer -b swarm-reviewer && git worktree add ../project-tester -b swarm-tester

--max-turns 70 (Qwen: --max-session-turns 70): short sessions on purpose. Every turn reads the whole context again, so one 200-turn session costs several times more than three of 70. A session that reaches the limit after doing something is a planned end, not a failure: the runner starts a fresh one at once and tells it to go on from git status and its subtasks.
mcp.json takes AGENT_ID and NETWORK_DIR from the environment (${AGENT_ID}); the runner sets them for every session.
--settings adds the agent-network hooks (new messages while working, no early stop); fill in its /abs/path values too, or drop the flag.
Prompt first, right after -p: --allowedTools takes several values and would swallow it.
instructionsFile (per agent, relative to this file): the agent's own instructions, appended to the standard prompt and read again before every session; can also be set on the page.
stream-json output lets the runner count tokens and cost per session (task statistics) and still show a readable log.

Lean context: a short system prompt ({systemPrompt} <- systemPromptFile) and only the tools the agent needs; every turn re-reads them, so this cuts tokens per turn several times. Skill is in --tools so the agents can load skills (java-dev-flow); drop it when they need none: every turn re-reads the skill list.

git: only the commands the protocol needs (status, diff, log, show, add, commit, merge, rev-parse); push, reset, checkout, branch -D are refused in -p. Add a command only when an agent really needs it.
Model: the command has {model}; "model" is the default (the tester runs on haiku), "models" is the choice in the runner card on the page (applies from the next session).
autostart: false = start that agent with the button on the page.

supervisor: the agent that looks after the others (page tab «Надзор»). A detector without a model checks the swarm every 10 s; on an incident (a question to you unanswered for questionAfterSec, a BLOCKED task, no progress for stallMin, the same command repeatCount times, a test JVM older than testMin, a runner that gave up) it starts one supervisor session with the tools of supervisor-mcp.json. Read-only file tools, no shell: it acts through the page (answers, messages, +rounds, handover) and frees hung tests and database locks; decisions only you can take come to the page as «нужно ваше решение». maxSessionsPerHour and budgetUsd (USD per 24 h) cap its cost; a quiet run costs nothing, one incident about $0.2–0.6 on sonnet. Switch it on/off, pick the model and its tools on the page.

supervisor.tools: your own commands for it, argv without a shell; {agentCwd} adds an agentId parameter (the agent's folder), {projectDir}/{networkDir} are filled in, own params are checked (type, enum, pattern). "action": true for a command that changes something: each run goes into its journal. disabledTools switches any tool off (also on the page).

schedules: tasks the page creates by itself on a cron (local time; @daily, @weekdays = Mon-Fri 9:00, ...), no model involved. A run is skipped while the previous task of the same schedule is still open. {date} and {time} in title/description are filled in. Off here ("enabled": false): switch it on on the Tasks tab or here.

Subagents: Agent in --tools lets an agent start subagents for bounded side jobs; --agents defines "helper" (read and run only, no swarm tools). Only the agent itself talks to the swarm: the built-in general-purpose subagent would inherit the agent-network tools, so the system prompt tells agents to use helper (or a project agent such as critic). Each subagent is a separate context: tokens. Drop Agent from --tools to switch subagents off.

command: {"helper": {"description": "A bounded side job for a swarm agent: search or read across many files, find why one test fails, review a diff. Reads and runs commands, changes nothing, reports back briefly.", "prompt": "You are a helper subagent of an agent in an agent-network swarm. Do exactly the job you were given and report back briefly: what you found, with file:line, and what you would do; nothing else. Never call agent-network tools (swarm_context, send_message, complete, subtasks, propose, approve, wait, ...): only the agent that started you talks to the swarm. Do not edit files. Keep command output short (tail, grep).", "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Bash"]}}

tools.name: surefire_failures
tools.description: Test report files with a failure or an error in an agent's folder (target/surefire-reports, failsafe-reports): read them with Read

tools.name: agent_git_log
tools.description: The latest 15 commits of an agent's worktree branch

tools.name: testcontainers
tools.description: Docker containers started by Testcontainers: id, image, how long they run, name

schedules.title: Flaky tests {date}
schedules.description: Run the full test suite twice (./mvnw -q -B verify -Dsurefire.timeout=900). Fix tests that fail only sometimes: shared state, ordering, time, ports, container reuse. Production code stays as it is unless a test proves a real bug; then ask the operator. In result: which tests were flaky, why, what you changed.
